# AI rules — Backend (Python 3.11+ • Flask 3.0)

Scope: `backend/**` — Flask REST API: blueprints in `routes/`, business logic in `services/`,
pytest suite in `tests/`. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) §4.1 for where this sits; this
file is the coding contract. The desktop app spawns this backend as a PyInstaller binary
([AI_ELECTRON.md](AI_ELECTRON.md)); web deployment runs it under gunicorn/supervisor
([AI_INFRA.md](AI_INFRA.md)). The frontend that calls it is governed by
[AI_FRONTEND.md](AI_FRONTEND.md).

## Layout & Contracts

- `routes/<name>.py` = HTTP layer only (Flask blueprints): validate the request, call a
  service, shape the JSON response. Routes never talk to external APIs directly.
- `services/<name>_service.py` = business logic. All external clients (OpenRouter, PyGithub,
  BookStack, pandoc subprocess) live in `services/` and nowhere else.
- `config.py` is the single place environment variables are read (python-dotenv). Services
  receive config values as arguments; no scattered `os.environ` lookups.
- Adding a config knob: `backend/config.py` → `.env.example` → `CONFIGURATION.md`, in the
  same change.
- Keep files ~800 lines or less; split services when they grow past it.
- No database/ORM in this project — don't introduce one without an explicit request.

## Style

- PEP8; type hints on public functions and routes; docstrings for public routes and services.
- API endpoints return JSON; web pages return HTML. Centralize HTTP error handlers (404, 500).
- Fail loudly and actionably on a missing prerequisite (API key, pandoc binary) — never
  silently degrade.
- Support both `backend.routes.x` and `routes.x` import styles only where PyInstaller
  packaging requires it (see AI_ELECTRON.md); don't spread the dual-import pattern further.

## Secrets & Environment

- Never hardcode secrets. `.env` (gitignored) for web; `electron-store` replaces it on desktop.
  `.env.example` is committed and stays in sync with `config.py`.
- Never log secrets or user document payloads.

## Testing (mandatory, gating)

- pytest is the gate: `backend/pytest.ini` enforces `--cov-fail-under=80` — the suite fails
  below 80% coverage. Don't lower it to make a run pass.
- Run: `source venv/bin/activate && cd backend && pytest` (root `venv/`, Python 3.11+).
- Structure: `tests/unit/` for services, `tests/integration/` for routes,
  `tests/fixtures/` for data and mock responses. Tests mirror the source layout.
- Mock **all** external APIs with `responses` / `pytest-mock` (OpenRouter, GitHub, BookStack,
  pandoc subprocess). Tests must never make a real OpenRouter call — it costs real money.
- Write tests for every new feature and bug fix **before** marking the work complete; every
  route gets at least a smoke test. TDD encouraged.
